# Roadmap: Alive Workplace 1.0 to 2.0

**Goal (owner, 2026-10-03): everything here, released, by 2026-10-17.** Speed matters most: another team could ship
first. Content quality is never cut: every feature is complete, looks vanilla-quality and feels finished. Lanes work
around the clock, several at once (`docs/agent/sessions.md`).

1. **1.0** (Milestones 22–26): builders that never need babysitting, finished visuals, performance at scale, and the
   public release. Ship it as soon as it's ready.
2. **The expansions** (Milestones 27–35), released in this order: 1.1 villages that build themselves, 1.2 Pokémon and
   villagers together, 1.3 Legends, 1.4 edicts and civic items, 1.5 quests become stories, 1.6 threats, 1.7 the
   realm, 1.8 classes and luxuries, 2.0 Wonders. Lanes build several at once; each release ships when its milestone
   is complete.

Everything done before this plan (Milestones 1–20, and the 0.137 work: fishing from boats, ferry rides, cavalry,
homes; about 215 items) is in `docs/roadmap-history.md`. Read it when you
need to know how something was built. The owner's decisions are at the bottom of this file. Don't change them
without asking.

## How to work this file

**Sprint mode** (owner, 2026-10-03). The mod's first 48,000 lines came from one chat in four days that built
features straight on `main` and released every hour; the claim/land/QA-every-hour setup that followed built one
feature in four days. So we work the way that chat did. Details: `docs/agent/sessions.md`, "Sprint mode".

- **Two build lanes split the roadmap by number:** lane a takes odd milestones and odd bugs, lane b even ones, so they
  never touch the same item. `sessions.py next --as <you>` lists yours, best first. The owner's chat takes anything.
- **Work straight on `main`.** No claims, branches, landings or handoff commits. Build a feature with its tests, tick
  it with `sessions.py done <id>` (add `--review` for something a player sees, after handing in its package), add the
  CHANGELOG line, run `./gradlew build`, and push the work and the tick in one commit. If the push is refused,
  `git pull --no-rebase` and push again (build again first only if the pull brought in code).
- **"Done when" is the spec.** Build all of it, art and builds included. If it can't be met as written, write the
  question in the Notes, ask through the digest, and take the next item. Don't invent the spec.
- **Bugs first, but only real ones.** Red CI and bugs a player would hit go into "Bugs" (`sessions.py bug`) and come
  first; a red `main` belongs to the lane on red duty (docs/agent/sessions.md, "Red main"). The QA lane runs hourly
  overnight and every 2 hours by day, and owns the bugs only a test or a scene sees.
- **Reviews never block work or releases.** A visible item's review package goes to the `reviews` branch
  (`sessions.py review`) and is marked `(review: pending)`; the digest sends it. A veto becomes a fix item.
- **His replies** are recorded with `sessions.py reply "<his words>" --as <you>`: `approve <ids>`,
  `veto <id>: <why>` (unticked, redone next), `change <id>: <what>` (a sub-item `<id>a`, done next).
- **Releases:** the evening digest releases every day when something new landed, even if `main` is red then: CI tags
  the first green build (minor bump for features, patch for fixes only). GitHub only; store pages wait for the owner.
- **Unfinished expansions stay switched off** behind their config switch until the milestone is complete; the release
  that ships the milestone turns it on.
- Items are numbered `<milestone>.<n>`, bugs `B<n>`; numbers are never reused.

Status marks: `[ ]` open · `(blocked: <why>)` · `[x] (review: pending <date>)` built, waiting for the owner ·
`[x] (approved <date>)` / `(approved auto <date>)` accepted · `(verified <date>)` tested by QA · `[ ] (vetoed <date>:
<why>)` to redo. Older marks (`claimed`, `paused`) come from the claim-and-land setup.

Related bugs filed: B25 [B17 still open via the job item], B26, B27.) Reassigning a worker can free someone else's workstation: Stations.assign and VillageHalls.assign release the old job site whenever a POI record exists there, without checking it is still the worker's own block. If the old block is broken far from its worker, the same kind of block is placed on that spot and another villager takes it, then the first worker is given a new job, the second worker's ticket is freed and two villagers can hold one block (vanilla's releasePoi shares the gap). Found by the 21.1a round-4 and B7 testers, untested. Done when: a GameTest of that sequence leaves the second worker's block taken. (found by night-1001-0646, 2026-10-01)

Test: the build workflow's duration on main, and the slowest batches in its GameTest log (found by lane-a-1006-0632, 2026-10-06) Status (qa-1009-2234): cause found. Friendship's look check (31.5, Friendship.lookedAt, every 10 ticks for every player) ray-casts with level.clip, which loads the chunk on the server thread when the player stands where no chunk is loaded. The suite's left-over mock players stand in such chunks (nothing moves their chunk tickets), so every tick gets slower the more tests have run: CI build 746 went from 5 ms a tick to 35 ms (runGameTest 108 min), and jstack put 64% of the server thread in Friendship.lookedAt ten minutes into a local run. Real players keep their chunks loaded, so nobody playing notices; only the suite does. Fix (mod, 3 lines, tried locally, not committed): in lookedAt, return null unless level.hasChunksAt(BlockPos.containing(eye), BlockPos.containing(end)). With it the same first 246 batches took 3.0 min instead of 8.0, no sample was in Friendship, and the 5 FriendshipGameTests still pass. Test: FriendshipLookQaGameTests.lookingFromAnUnloadedChunkLoadsNothing on tests/friendship-look-chunks-1009 (fails on main, passes with the fix); merge that branch with the fix, then check one full build is back near 15 min. Until then the nightly tests and the showcase are cancelled at their time limits every night (no flake sweep, log audit, pack boot or soak since 2026-10-06), and `ship`'s full build doesn't fit a QA run.

Found (the run's junit and job log): the timing check failed, not the floating-block one: crew 4,140 ticks against a limit of 3,336 (lone builder 12,131); stage III's STRUCTURE took 2,085 ticks (stages I and II 1,100 and 790), and the log has 'Builder stalled 30 s: ... stage_3_0 ... STRUCTURE, status WORKING, 104 placed, 0 skipped, 0 kinds missing', the same part, count and stage as B254's failure. So the lead's retry pass on stage III stood still 30 s or more with nothing given up yet (a give-up during retries counts as skipped), then went on: the dome's centre tile over the 1-high gap above stage II's roof (B254) is the likely block, and the wait is one of BuilderWork's crew waits during retries (crewHasWork/crewBlocked postpone with no tick limit while the block under is deferred but not given up; GIVEN_UP_WAIT only covers a given-up block under). Mod side: a player would see a Wonder crew stand idle 30-60 s near the dome's top; the folly still finishes. Not seen in 12 more runs (2 sets of 6 copies, all passed, stage III retries short). Done: the test now notes each 30-second stall of a part (placed, given up, cursor, retries left, the lead's spot and block, the cursor block and the one under it, each member's spot and block) in its timing and unfinished messages and in the log ('B326 crew stall'), so the next failure names the waiting block. Next: with that note, bound the wait that held (or let a crew member lay the deferred block under the cursor). Status (lane-a-1023-0622): fixed. Cause (read in BuilderWork): during the lead's retry pass two postpones had no tick bound: a block crewBlocked (a member holds its column or claims it, or it is too high, or the block under is not there and not given up) was postponed every tick for as long as that held (helperWait bounds only the claim case, and crewBlocked short-circuits it), and a SKIP block waited while crewHasWork, which counts the very blocks waiting on it. A member that holds the column of the block under (it keeps walking for a block it can't reach; members can't put up scaffolding) left the lead idle with nothing given up, the 104 placed, 0 skipped stall. Fix: once the crew has stood still GIVEN_UP_WAIT (200 ticks) while retrying, the lead takes the cursor's block over (BuilderWork.takeOver: the member on its column or block lets it go, the lead takes the column) if what goes under it is there, so never a block in the air (B254); a block waiting on one under it still waits, and the lead takes that one in turn; and a SKIP block is no longer postponed then (deferred, so given up, as a lone builder's). Nothing saved changes (the stand-still counter is transient, restarted after a load). Test: WonderCrewGameTests.aColumnAMemberHoldsAndNeverLaysIsTakenOverByTheLead (a test hut as a Wonder part, one wall block and the one over it missing, a member holding that column for good): failed without the fix (still retrying after 2,400 ticks, 2 retries left, 0 given up), passes with it; with it, 168 tests of WonderCrew, BuilderCrew, Builder, BuilderChaos, BuildersShareSpare, Scaffolding, WonderSite and WonderGardens passed. Not proven to be the exact CI wait (not reproduced there); the stall note from lane-a-1023-0322 stays in the folly test to name it if it comes back.

CI's message: 'the villager is none (job site Optional.empty)', the villager alive at (3, 2, 5) of the Library (on the edge of the furnished desk), its pick and walk target the lectern at (6, 1, 9), not moving. Cause: Carved Wood's lantern says a land path may go through it (vanilla's lantern says no: the default for a block that isn't a full cube is yes), so the path finder counted the cell of the lantern standing on the Handcrafted desk as walkable; the villager's path to the lectern went up onto the desk and through the lantern, it jumped onto the desk, couldn't pass the lantern and stood on the desk's edge walking on the spot till the test timed out. Reproduced: a jobless villager spawned on the desk's edge stuck 3 of 10 spots (5,400 ticks, never moving); the probe showed the lantern cell WALKABLE, isPathfindable true. Fix (mod): work/PathObstacles, from WalkNodeEvaluatorMixin beside B156's trapdoors: a cell with a block that calls itself passable but whose collision is inside the villager's body above its step height is BLOCKED to a villager's path (carpets, beds, ladders, open doors stay walkable; doors, trapdoors and gates keep vanilla's rules). Tests: aVillagersPathGoesRoundACarvedWoodLanternOnADesk (fails without the fix: the path ran over the desk) and aVillagersPathStillCrossesACarpet; the Library test's message now also prints the villager's exact position, what it stands on and its path. Evidence: desk-edge spawns 10 of 10 took a lectern job with the fix; the Library test repeated 180 times (30 + 150, each in its own batch) all passed; on the final code (with the body guards) runGameTest 2650/2650 passed, and runCompatGameTest narrowed to CarvedStylesCompatTests plus 60 Library repeats and 10 of each path test passed 86/86 (a full compat run in this container was killed for memory, exit 137, not a test failure).

- [ ] **B427** Red main: QaRequestsLeaderboardGameTests.joiningAtExactlyThreeHeartsAndJustUnder (new test, pulled 2026-10-25) fails 'Dara has nothing to ask' in CI build 1733 on 6e95c9d and in a local full build of d4166c2 (1 of 3173); expected: passes, or a real bug in personal requests at exactly three hearts. Test: QaRequestsLeaderboardGameTests on main (found by lane-e-1025-0112, 2026-10-25) Again (lane-e-1025-0413, local full build of 92dd0dd, whose CI build 1748 was green): joiningAtExactlyThreeHeartsAndJustUnder 'Dara has nothing to ask' and, in the same class, theGiverDiesMidRequest 'Dara has no level_up to ask' (2 of 3176): both look like a flake in how the class picks Dara's request, not personal requests themselves. Both local builds had lane E's new QaConfigExtremesGameTests in; that class and this one pass together (18 of 18), so it isn't the cause as far as tested; it waits on branch qa/config-extremes-1025 for a green full build (ship it with sessions.py ship once this flake is fixed). Status (lane-a-1025-0622): not found yet. Both failures come from the first PersonalRequests.resolve of a level_up for a fresh Dara (only two conditions, hearts_at_least 3 and level_below 5, can make it null), so either Friendship.add(…, 300) didn't take (Friendship.ENABLED off or Dara not eligible: no hall found by CivicEffects.hallOf / VillageHalls.nearest) or her farmer job didn't stick. Not reproduced: 120 isolated repeats of joining, theGiverDies and aHelperWhoLeft (each its own batch) all passed, and two local full runs passed both (one failed only on qaSandrampEdge's raider test, a different flake). In CI the two failures followed different tests (BuilderGameTests' materials-from-another-chest; SiegeGameTests' director), so it isn't one neighbour. Flags can't leak across batches (one test a batch; resets run before the next test starts) and nothing ticks between worker() and resolve, so the leading suspect is the hall's point of interest not being found at callback time. The failure messages now print what the conditions saw (PersonalRequestGameTests.why: friendship/requests switches, points, hall of the villager, nearest hall, the block and point of interest at HALL, radius, job, game time), so the next failure names the cause. Status (lane-a-1027-0923): not reproduced, and the leading suspect is ruled out by the 1.21.1 bytecode: ServerLevel.onBlockStateChange files a POI through server.execute, which on the server thread outside a task runs at once (BlockableEventLoop.execute → scheduleExecutables false), so the hall's point of interest is in the moment helper.setBlock returns (HeartEventGameTests.village's comment "goes in after the tick" is wrong; the 2-tick wait is harmless). Also ruled out: another batch's after-hooks resetting flags after this test starts (GameTestTicker iterates a CopyOnWriteArrayList snapshot, so a new batch starts the tick after the old one's listeners ran); a stale hall POI nearer Dara (every block change, structure clearing included, goes through onBlockStateChange synchronously); game-time caches (VillageHalls.nearest, CivicEffects.HALLS: game time only moves forward, QaWarParty's setGameTime too); HostileSpawns.REFUSED_FOR_TESTS (hostiles, golems and pets only); quest-file swaps (QuestFiles.load in QuestEngine and QaQuestJournal restore the real set). Note CivicEffects.HALLS is a WeakHashMap keyed by Villager, whose equals/hashCode go by entity id (unique per JVM, so harmless). What's left is Friendship.ENABLED false at the callback, Dara not alive, or her job not set; the why() line of the next failure tells which. Nothing changed in code.

- [x] **B476** (approved 2026-10-26) (verified 2026-10-26: re-read against their specs: QaDenHelperBugTests [4: unloaded helper still hired, a day later sent home and told, a helper no longer a trainer leaves] and QaDenHelperRaidBugTests [2: raid joined by the Raid Dens statistic is struck and its loss ends the hiring; raid found by the helpers' own look on real ticks, kept over a save] pass in 3 full compat runs this session [734-735 of 734-735]) Player-visible (38.1a, docs/design/M38.md 'Boss damage is built'): hired raid helpers never strike the boss of a real raid, and a lost raid keeps them hired for the rest of the day. Raid Dens awards raids_joined as the player enters the raid, so RaidHelpers.statAwarded calls joined(level, hire, player, null) first: hire.joined is set with no raid id, and the helpers' own look (tick: 'if (!hire.joined && ... now % 20 == 0)', the only path that stores raid.get().id()) never runs again, so hire.raid stays null and the strike/WON/LOST block ('if (hire.raid != null && now >= hire.nextStrike)') is skipped for good. Expected: after a join by the statistic the helpers find the player's raid (RaidAssist.raidOf) and keep its id, so they wear the boss down to a quarter and go home when it's lost. Also: that look needs gameTime % 20 == 0 inside a server-tick handler that runs only when getTickCount() % 5 == 0; the two counters differ by the world's age, so in most worlds (offset not a multiple of 5) the look never fires at all. Test: QaDenHelperRaidBugTests.aRaidJoinedAsRaidDensTellsItIsStruckAndItsLossSeen on tests/raid-helper-stat-join (fails: 'the helpers never struck its boss (health 400.0 of 400, the hiring's raid null)'). Test: QaTrainStationSameName1104eCompatTests#bothStationsGivenTheSameNameStillCarryTheCaravan (on main); repeat it with ALIVEWORKPLACE_REPEAT=QaTrainStationSameName1104eCompatTests#bothStationsGivenTheSameNameStillCarryTheCaravan ALIVEWORKPLACE_REPEAT_TIMES=8 and only_tests.py --compat RepeatNewTests (found by lane-e-1104-1013, 2026-11-04) Again (lane-e-1105-0412): the only failure of a local full build on main 190d65021 + one QA class (compat 1183 of 1184, 05:38Z). Status (lane-a-1107-0623): fixed. Cause: Create's DestinationInstruction collects every station whose name fits the stop and Navigation.findPathTo takes the nearest; when that is the station the train stands at, ScheduleRuntime.tick counts the stop as reached (IN_TRANSIT, destinationReached) and the train waits there for the other station's stop, round after round. Whether Create's search finds the station under the train depends on exactly where the train stopped, hence 1 run in 8. Fix: CreateTrains.sendOn (called from follow, every hall look at its train): a train of the village's schedule in POST_TRANSIT at a station that fits its stop's name but isn't the stop's station (by GlobalStation id) is given Create's own path to the stop's station (Navigation.findPathTo(station) + startNavigation, state IN_TRANSIT), the way ScheduleRuntime starts a trip; no names change and nothing new is saved. Test: TrainStationsOneNameCompatTests (2 tests: both stations renamed 'Station' while the train stands at home and at the other village, with Create's namesake outcome forced, so the bad case happens every run; both failed without the fix with 'POST_TRANSIT #0/#1 at Station', as in the report); RepeatNewTests x8 of those two and QaTrainStationSameName1104eCompatTests#bothStationsGivenTheSameNameStillCarryTheCaravan: 24 of 24 passed (the QA test hit the bad case naturally in 2 of its 8 runs and recovered). All 27 Create train compat classes: 84 of 85 passed, the one failure B940's known 'logs 96 of 64' flake in TrainStationNamesApartCompatTests (sendOn never fired for that train). - [ ] **B1038** Player-visible (Scan Tool and imported or Structure Block blueprints, builders): a block scanned in the middle of a moment is built frozen in it for good. The Scan Tool saves with fillFromWorld, so a wooden pressure plate a villager stood on (powered=true), a button just pressed, a big dripleaf tipped under someone (tilt=full) or a sculk sensor that just heard a step (sculk_sensor_phase=active) is in the blueprint that way; the Builder places that state with no tick pending (MaterialRules.emptied doesn't reset these, and 'powered' only counts as volatile for matching), so the plate and button power what's beside them forever (a door by the plate stays open), the leaf stays tipped (a player falls through it) and the sensor never hears again. ## Milestone 27: Villages that build themselves (1.1)

Items in Milestones 27–35 sometimes point at another milestone's item by name ("M29's Seer item"): find it there.

You paint your village's plan once on a **City Plan** (homes here, workshops there, a market, gardens, roads, a wall),
and a new villager, the **Steward**, grows the village into it: every morning he compares the plan with what the
village lacks (the numbers behind the hall's "What next?" tips) and lines up the right building, in the right zone and
the zone's style, for the village's builders. You approve each plan with one click at the hall, or let the village run
itself; roads with lamps and bridges link the buildings and the villages you trade with, walls go up once raids start,
and an old vanilla village slowly rebuilds itself one house at a time. It answers the top complaint about colony mods
(babysitting) and builds on the builder (`BuildSite`, styles, upgrades, `Paths`), the Village Hall (census,
`VillageAdvice`, ranks, research) and `Caravans`.

  Steward's day, his desk on the hall's screen, roads, walls, renewed houses), the data formats with one example file
  each (zone kinds, Steward rules, road styles, wall kits, renewal lists), the config switches, every new saved field

## Milestone 28: Pokémon and villagers, together (1.2)

Pokémon stop being a side mod and become part of village life. Pokémon pastured by a workstation are seen at work (a
Machamp shouldering beams to the builder, a Wartortle watering the fields, a Pidgeotto off with the air mail), five new
jobs work Cobblemon's own blocks, villages get a Pokémon Center, and every festival of a village with an Arena
becomes the Festival Cup: a themed tournament its trade partners send their Trainer Leaders to, with the stands full, a
fair on, and the winner's banner flying over the winning village. It builds on `work/Partners`, `compat/cobblemon/`,
`trainer/`, `hall/Festivals`, `MarketDays`, `Caravans` and the `Chronicle`; the owner's pack is still on Cobblemon 1.7.3,
so the parts that need Cobblemon 1.8 (Habitat Blocks, Type Gems, Alphas) wait quietly until the pack moves up. Nothing
here adds a new kind of speed bonus (the new jobs get the partners' existing one).

## Milestone 29: Legends: rare villagers (1.3)

One-of-a-kind villagers, earned and never bought, each changing what a village can do: about one villager in thirty is
Gifted with a rare trait, and above them stand twelve Legends, Rare (one per village), Legendary (one per world) or
Mythic (several per server, capped per village by its rank, announced to everyone). Legends come only when a village
has earned them, in four ways: as guests (Terraria-style), found out in the world, born to two schooled Masters, or
inspired by a strange mood to make a Masterwork. Each wants a tier III home of their own, a luxury they like and a
happy village, and an unhappy Legend never leaves but goes on strike. It builds on people/ (Traits, Moods, Families,
Homes, Couples), inn/ (Innkeepers), school/ (Schools), hall/ (VillageRanks, Chronicle, Festivals, Treasury, Caravans,
MarketDays) and research/.

  server owners can add their own. A file holds: `rarity` (`rare`, `legendary`, `mythic`); `job` (the trade they work,
  always as a Master, with every level's trades through `Schools.headStart`; `aliveworkplace:legend` for Legends
  without one); `title`, `lore` and six `names` (lang keys, for guests; a villager who becomes a Legend keeps their
  own name); `conditions` (what the village must have); `arrive` (the ways they come, each with its settings:
  29.7-29.10); `needs` (29.5); `powers`; `masterwork` (29.10); `outfit` (a texture, 29.4). The shared toolbox, one

    `caravan_routes`, `meal_kinds`, `festival_crowd`, `animals_at_job` (animals within 16 blocks of a trade's
    workstations), `research_levels`, `iron_golems`, `full_moon`, `first_city` and `legend` (a given Legend settled

## Milestone 30: Edicts and civic items (1.4)

The village gets laws and landmarks. A Book of Edicts in the Village Ledger lets the hall's owner proclaim one edict
per rank (Frostpunk-style): each gives the village a real boost at a real cost, and each has a reform the village earns
through the hall's quests, which keeps the boost and drops the cost for that village for good. Civic items, each an
item of its own (the Cradle, the Work Horn, the Village Banner, the Harvest Idol, Guild Charters with their
Guildhalls, and six tonics from the alchemist and the chef), give players more ways to shape a village. It builds on
the Village Hall (`VillageNeeds`, `VillageQuests`, `VillageRanks`, `Festivals`, `Treasury`), `people/Moods` and
`BuilderLevels.delay`, and adds the one shared cap that stops all speed bonuses together at twice normal pace.

## Milestone 31: Quests become stories (1.5)

The village's people become people you know. Each named villager keeps a friendship with each player (gifts, favours,
heart events that tell their life story) and asks friends for help with their own goals; each village gives each
player a standing and a title; a bounty board hangs up wanted posters; and story arcs run in chapters over days: The
Bandit King, The Sickness, The Lost Caravan and The Professor's Thesis. It builds on the hall's daily quests
(`hall/VillageQuests`), the chronicle, `people/` (names, chatter, couples, families, moods), `guard/BanditCamps`,
`hall/Caravans` and `people/Sickness`. Everything a player can be asked to do is a data file, so server owners can
write their own stories; nothing waits forever on a player.

## Milestone 32: Threats worth building walls for (1.6)

Raids today are monsters or bandits walking in at night, and walls do little more than shut their gates. In 1.6 every
land has its own enemy camped nearby under a named captain (pillager warbands with rams and ladders, drowned pirates
from the sea, desert raiders under a pharaoh, piglins through a portal, a witch coven's hexes) who lay sieges that
walls, gates, towers and archers decide, while a watchtower gives a day's warning and scouts, guards and hired swords
let the player strike back at their camps. Fire, drought and plague each get a job that answers them, and every threat
has a switch and a peaceful setting. It builds on guard/VillageRaids, BanditCamps, Gates, GuardRally, Mercenaries, the
Rally Banner and the defence blueprints (tools/blueprints/defence.py).

## Milestone 33: From village to realm (1.7)

Villages stop being islands. Each one becomes known for what its land and workers make and short of what they don't,
caravans carry those goods at prices that move with supply and demand, a City sends settlers to found a sister village
wherever you point on the map, and linked villages become a realm with a capital, a treasury, shared research and
guards who ride to each other's aid. Between players come trade pacts, alliances, a weekly leaderboard in chat, and
feuds that only turn to war on a PvP server. It all builds on what exists: hall/Caravans, the Village Ledger and
treasury, travel posts, mail, village protection and the Settler's Wagon (camp/).

Trade
  goods are data: `data/aliveworkplace/trade_goods/<good>.json`, loaded through `Platform.onDataReload` so datapacks
  and `/reload` work. One file is one good: its name key and icon, its items (an item or an item tag), a bundle size,
  a base price in hundredths of an emerald a bundle, `made_by` (professions and biome tags), `wanted_in` (biome tags,
  and professions that use it), and optional events that raise demand for a few days (after a raid, while villagers
  are ill). Once a day, in the hall's round, each village works out up to 3 goods it's **known for** (2 points for
  each worker of a making job, up to 6; 3 if the hall stands in a making biome; 1 if its Storehouses hold two bundles
  or more; 4 points to count) and up to 3 it's **short of** (3 if its biome wants it; 1 for each worker of a job that
  uses it, up to 3; 2 if a worker is waiting for it on the requests board; 1 if the Storehouses hold less than a
  bundle; 4 points to count); a good is never both. Every good also gets a **price** there: its base times 1 + 0.2 ×
  (demand − supply), kept between half and twice the base (supply: bundles in the Storehouses, up to 5, plus 3 if
  known for it; demand: 3 if short of it, plus bundles workers are waiting for, up to 3, plus 2 for food while the
  store is under 16 meals, plus any event's). Each dawn a price moves a third of the way toward that. All of it is
  kept on the village's `Caravans.Data` entry (new keys, empty until the next round), so a village that isn't loaded
  keeps its last prices. Six test goods ship in the gametest datapack, not in the game. Config `villageEconomy`. Done
  when:
  - GameTests: three lumberjacks by a hall in a forest make it known for the test timber; a desert hall whose builder
    waits for logs is short of it; no good is both; a price moves a third of the way each dawn and stays between half
    and twice its base; a raid event raises demand for its days only;
  - the new keys survive save and reload, and a village entry saved before this item loads with empty lists;
  - with `villageEconomy` off nothing is worked out and `caravansCarryWhatAnotherVillageNeeds` passes unchanged.

  can let a member go. A realm's rank comes from its members: **Barony** (2 villages), **County** (3, the capital a

  distance, owner; the capital with a crown) and the realm's arms: click it with a banner to set them (they fly on
  relief riders' shields and colour the realm's map banners and caravans). The hall's name icon says which realm the

## Milestone 34: Classes and luxuries (1.8)

Villages get a social ladder, as in Anno 1800 and Manor Lords: a household rises from **Peasant** to **Artisan**,
**Burgher** and **Noble** when its needs are met (a better house, a varied diet, services nearby and, higher up,
luxuries from four new trades: the Vintner, Tailor, Printer and Jeweller), and falls back when they aren't. Higher
classes pay more into the treasury, open higher jobs, dress the part and want grander houses; grown villagers age
into elders who retire and teach, and every family has a tree. It builds on `people/` (`Homes`, `Diet`, `Moods`,
`Families`, `Couples`), `hall/VillageNeeds` and the `Treasury`, `craft/CrafterWork` and the outfit pipeline, and it
switches on for every village of the owner's live server at once, so it ends with a careful migration and a rehearsal
on a real world.

  "id": "aliveworkplace:work_clothes"}], "wants": [...]}`. The toolbox of need types (`people/ClassNeeds`): `home`
  (the grade of the building their bed is in, `Homes`), `fed_days`, `diet` (`Diet`), `beauty` (decorations within 16

  lifts them one class; a need of their own class unmet `classFallDays` (3) dawns running drops them one, never below
  Peasant; one step a day at most. Config `villageClasses` (on), off in GameTests unless a test turns it on. The

  "aliveworkplace:berry_wine", "count": 1, "min_age_days": 3}], "output": {"id": "aliveworkplace:vintage_wine"},
  "ticks": 200}`. A new `Crafting.Kind.LUXURY` plans from these files (makings by item or tag; vanilla makings up to
  the usual two steps down), and `craft/LuxuryWork` (a `CrafterWork`, like `ChefWork`) makes, in turn, whatever the
  village store holds fewer than 8 of, from its own chests, the store and the village's stashes, stock orders first
  (`StockOrders`). Goods that age carry the day they were made (a `made_day` data component; the tooltip says
  "Pressed on day 42 · vintage in 2 days"). Missing makings go on the requests board; Craftsmanship research speeds
  the makers like the other crafters. Done when: `LuxuryWorkGameTests` with test recipes: a maker makes what's short
  and stops at 8, keeps to its level, waits for an aged input (the day moved on in the test), asks for missing
  makings on the board, fills a stock order first, and a datapack recipe adds a new good with no code. Nothing to see
  yet: `--no-review`.

## Milestone 35: Wonders (2.0)

A Wonder is a village's life's work: a huge build raised in four stages by every builder in the village at once, fed
by goods from every job, drawn up by the Master Architect and needing another Legend. Each of the eight Wonders (the
Great Cathedral, the Lighthouse, the Great Library, the Great Wall, the Observatory, the Hanging Gardens, the Colossus
and the Stadium) changes what its village or its whole realm can do, and their time-lapses are the 2.0 trailers. It
builds on the builder (`BuildSite`, `BuildSiteManager`, `BuilderWork`'s helpers, `Upkeep`), the blueprint generator
(`tools/blueprints/`, STYLE.md), the Village Hall (ranks, research, festivals, caravans, the chronicle) and M29's
Legends.

## Milestone 37: Furnished homes and modded storage (2.1)

Builds use the pack's furniture mods when they're installed: Handcrafted chairs round a Handcrafted table, Lucky's
Cozy Home sofas and clocks, CobbleFurnies' Poké Ball chairs and stoves, Beautify's blinds, picture frames and
candelabras, and Carved Wood's and Rechiseled's decorative blocks; with none of them installed, every build is the
plain vanilla build it is today. Villagers sit on the chairs and sleep in the fancy beds. Porters, the Storehouse and
every job that reads chests also work with Sophisticated Storage (chests, barrels, controllers) and Tom's Simple
Storage (connectors and terminals). It ships as **2.1**, behind its own flag `Expansions.M37` (off on `main` until the
release that completes it). Support goes by block and item ids, tags and data files only, never the mods' classes;
the mods stay optional (`suggests`). What's there already: Handcrafted 4.0.3, Beautify 2.0.0, CobbleFurnies 1.2,
Carved Wood 1.9.7-B, Rechiseled 1.2.4, Sophisticated Storage 1.3.7.9 and Tom's Simple Storage 2.3.0 are in the compat
test runtime (`tests.compat_mods` in `stonecutter.properties.toml`), and `PackModsCompatTests` builds a sample of each
mod's blocks and uses a Sophisticated barrel as a supply chest; `ItemStores` reads storage through Fabric's transfer
API; `build/ModdedBlocks.STORAGE_NETWORK` keeps Sophisticated controllers and links and every Tom's block but the
filing cabinet out of the supply chests, so nothing counts twice. Lucky's Cozyhome Refurnished 1.1.20 can't load in
the dev runtime (its `getItems()` clashes with a Mojang-mapped name), so Cozyhome is checked by the pack test
(`tools/packtest/run.sh`, the real pack) only. Depends on: M26 (the builds and their interiors as they stand at 1.0);
M34's grander homes get furnished too, and simply aren't there until M34 is on.

## Milestone 38: Cobblemon depth (2.2)

Three of the pack's Pokémon mods come into village life. **Raid Dens** (Cobblemon Raid Dens): the village knows the
dens around it, its guards stand watch at them and its trainers challenge them, bringing raid loot home. **Mega
Evolution** (Mega Showdown): more of the village's trainers Mega Evolve, players see who can, and the village can make
Mega Stones and Key Stones. **Cobblecuisine**: the Chef, the Camp Cook and the farmers cook and grow its dishes, which
count for the villagers' diet and feed the partners. It ships as **2.2**, behind its own flag `Expansions.M38` (off on
`main` until the release that completes it). It builds on `compat/cobblemon/` (`CobblemonMegas`, `CobblemonTrainers`,
`CobblemonCampPot`, `CobblemonPartners`), `trainer/`, the Stadium (35.x), `craft/Chefs`, `people/Diet` and M28/M34's
jobs. The mods are optional: their ids, tags, data files and advancements only, each behind `isModLoaded`, and any
Cobblemon class only in `compat/cobblemon/`. What the jars hold (read from `build/packtest/server/mods`):
Raid Dens 0.11.3: the den block `cobblemonraiddens:raid_crystal_block` (states `is_active`, `raid_tier` `tier_one` to
`tier_seven`, `raid_type`, `can_reset`, `is_natural`), placed by its world generation in
`#cobblemonraiddens:raid_spawnable` biomes, raids fought in its own dimension, bosses in
`data/cobblemonraiddens/raid/boss/<species>.json` (tier, type, weight), loot in
`data/cobblemonraiddens/loot_table/raid/tier/<tier>.json`, items `raid_shard` (and `_50`, `_100`), `raid_pouch`,
`cheer_attack`, `cheer_defense`, `cheer_heal`, `catching_charm`, advancements `cobblemonraiddens:join_raid` and
`tier_one` to `tier_seven`. Mega Showdown 1.8.4 (already in the compat runtime; Master trainers already hold a Mega
Stone and Mega Evolve, `MegaCompatTests`): `mega_showdown:keystone`, the `#mega_showdown:mega_bracelet` and
`#mega_showdown:mega_stone` tags, `keystone_ore`, `mega_stone_crystal`, `pedestal`, the `mega_meteorid_*` blocks.
Cobblecuisine 2.0.1: 178 items, 236 plain crafting recipes from vanilla and Cobblemon ingredients (mints, berries),
the `cobblecuisine:bean_crop` block and six colours of beans (`#cobblecuisine:beans`). Depends on: M28 (trainers,
partners, the Camp Cook), M34 (the Jeweller, luxuries) and M35 (the Stadium), each with a fallback here.

## Milestone 39: Create integration (2.3)

Villages go mechanical with Create: a Mechanic villager keeps the machines turning, villagers feed millstones,
presses, mixers and crushing wheels to process the village's goods into the store, builders raise watermills,
windmills and belt-line workshops and build working contraptions from a blueprint, Create schematics load at the
Blueprint Table, and later trains link villages for caravans. It ships as **2.3**, behind its own flag
`Expansions.M39` (off on `main` until the release that completes it). The owner made his own Fabric 1.21.1 port of
Create and will provide the jar (owner, 2026-10-17), so every item waits on it and stays at the level that doesn't
depend on the port's internals. As with every mod: block and item ids, tags, recipe types and data files only, behind
`isModLoaded`, the mod in `suggests`, and a compat test for each item. Create's usual ids (`create:millstone`,
`create:mechanical_press`, `create:mechanical_mixer`, `create:basin`, `create:crushing_wheel`, `create:water_wheel`,
`create:windmill_bearing`, `create:shaft`, `create:cogwheel`, `create:large_cogwheel`, `create:belt`,
`create:depot`, `create:track_station`, `create:schematic`) are to be confirmed against the port in 39.1. Depends on:
the owner's port jar; M33's caravans (39.7).

  millstone (wheat to flour), the Smith's mechanical press (ingots to sheets), the Chef's mixer and basin (dough), the
  Miner's crushing wheels (ores to crushed ore). What a machine makes is read from Create's own recipe types by id
  (`create:milling`, `create:pressing`, `create:mixing`, `create:crushing`) through the recipe manager; the worker
  takes the input from the store, feeds the machine, collects the output to the store, and works only while the
  machine turns. Done when: compat GameTests per machine (input fed, output in the store, nothing fed while it's
  stopped, a full store pauses it, a save and reload mid-job finishes it); scene `create_mill`.

  (a mechanical harvester and plough on a belt, a water wheel), a **Clock Tower** (a cuckoo clock and shafts, a
  purely decorative build with a working mechanism) and a **Pump House** (a mechanical pump, pipes and a fluid tank
  in a small brick house). Each is original, in the mod's styles (`STYLE.md`), checked in renders with the architect
  skill; its machine turns when built (the 39.4 test's way). Done when: the six builds with renders; compat
  GameTests: each builds with nothing skipped and its machine turns (speed read from block entity data by name), hidden
  without Create; text, wiki and guide pages; scene `create_builds_more`.

## Later (not in this plan)

- The 26.x node (Milestone 19, phases 3–4): on hold until the owner says go.

## Design decisions (from the owner)

- **Create** (2026-10-18): real trains, the way Create intends (39.7a); the Mechanic never fixes players' own Create
  machines, only the village's. **Builds** (2026-10-18): two libraries, vanilla and modded (37.12); the old builds
  are kept, not deleted. **Table** (2026-10-18): no description lines, only "Jobs: …" and "Beds: N" (36.6a).

- **Post-1.0 answers** (2026-10-18): Raid Dens of tier 4 and up are for players only (village trainers up to tier 3,
  38.4); the Mega Bracelet is given once per player per realm (38.5); furniture defaults to Handcrafted first, then
  Cozy Home, CobbleFurnies, Beautify (37.3); homes with a Pokémon partner get CobbleFurnies' Poké Ball chair and desk
  (37.4).
- **The Blueprint Table is a collection** (2026-10-15, 26.10): unlocked builds in colour (Get Blueprint as before),
  locked ones greyed out with how to get them, rare ones (Wonders, the builder-only grander homes, other special
  builds) a hidden "???" until found; the preview still shows a locked build, dimmed. The basics start unlocked (about
  15 to 20, a data list); unlocks belong to the village; existing villages keep everything standing or being built;
  imports, uploads and scans are always unlocked; expansion gates still apply. Five ways to unlock: buying from a
  builder, builder level-ups, questbook rewards, blueprints found in loot (used on the Table), market-day traders. A
  server switch, `blueprintUnlocks`, default on.
- **Playtest asks go in 1.0** (2026-10-14): retraining an employed villager for emeralds at our job blocks (26.6), a
  chest that shows what the build still needs (26.7), and a start-to-finish questbook as FTB Quests chapters (26.8).
- **Everything ships at once in 1.0** (2026-10-13): every expansion (1.1 to 2.0) is done but 30.22, so 1.0 turns them all
  on together (every `Expansions.M27`..`M35` flag), and the server updates once. Before that: 0.144.0 pre-release
  (2026-10-13, all flags still off), a pass through the wiki, every known bug fixed (the showcase's failing scenes
  included), 25.4's soak at the earliest run, then 26.4. Publishing (26.5) is approved for when we feel ready. A
  village's first day doesn't count against the 15% tick target (30.22). No owner signature builds (23.9 dropped).
- **Unfinished expansions stay off** (2026-10-05, after 0.139.0 shipped 1.1-1.4 switched on): each expansion is
  switched off until the whole of it (e.g. all of 1.1) is done; the release that completes it turns it on (B76).
- Target **Fabric 1.21.1** to match the Cobbleverse pack. The mod is needed on both the server and the clients.
- **Builders are the priority.** Giving villagers jobs is the core of the mod.
- Trainers: normal villagers get a Trainer job at different levels, and **level up as you battle them** (like trading).
  They range from really easy to extremely difficult. **No badges and no gym leaders.** Each village gets a **Trainer
  Leader** that starts difficult and pays money only.
- Cobblemon integration must be optional.
- License: GPL-3.0-or-later (lets us adapt MineColonies code, which is GPL-3.0-or-later, with attribution).
- Builds from the internet come in as files (.litematic/.schem/.nbt); we don't scrape sites. Only ship our own
  original builds.
- Villagers act as a cohesive unit (Milestone 6). Automatic where possible. Keyed on blocks, never on a particular
  structure, because packs add their own villages. Village farmers harvest into nearby chests.
- *My NPCs* does some of what we want "in a different way" the owner doesn't love. Rebuild the roles that fit the pack
  as villager jobs, not as admin-configured NPCs.
- **As big as MineColonies, if not bigger** (2026-09-28; since 2026-10-03 the plan itself, Milestones 27–35), built in
  parts. Ideas can come from MineColonies (GPL-3.0;
  code only adapted with attribution). What stays ours: it runs on Fabric 1.21.1 in the pack, works with the villagers
  and villages already in the world, and Cobblemon runs through every part.
- **Builds should look sleek and interesting** (2026-09-29). Every build we ship follows `tools/blueprints/STYLE.md` and
  is checked in a render first. Open-source builds may be used only if their licence allows it and they're credited.
- **Village protection** (2026-09-29): a setting on the Village Hall, off unless its owner turns it on.
- **Multi-version** (2026-09-29): follow the minecraft-mod-engineer skill. Keep today's feature packages; no partial
  26.3 release; jar names `<ver>+<mc>`.
- **Textures** (2026-09-29; replaces "no new pixel art for now"): all texture, item, outfit and GUI art goes through the
  owner's minecraft-pixel-art skill (recipes in `tools/textures/art`, drawn by `tools/textures/generate.py`), and he
  approves it in review packages. **Each thing is drawn the way vanilla draws its kind**: a book lies on the diagonal
  like vanilla's books, a tool follows vanilla's tools, a map vanilla's maps, a workstation is built from its
  material's tile like the crafting table.
- **1.0 first** (2026-09-29): the next goal is a public 1.0, polished rather than bigger. Priorities: builders and
  blueprints, then visuals and textures, then performance at scale.
- **Review after every job** (2026-09-29): after each finished item, playtest with the bot and send a review package.
  The owner approves or vetoes. Work continues while he reviews, but only approved work is released.
- **Fewer job blocks** (2026-09-30): too many job blocks look ugly and put new players off. Jobs use vanilla blocks
  wherever one fits (a jukebox for the bard, a beehive for the beekeeper); jobs that are close share a block, and the
  player picks the job by right-clicking the villager with an item. Custom job blocks only where nothing vanilla will
  do, such as the Blueprint Table. The plan is under 21.1a.
- **Hands-off** (2026-09-29): the owner reviews only what he can see or feel in game, from screenshots and GIFs.
  Work with nothing to see (tests, tooling, internal fixes) is accepted automatically once the tester passes, and is
  only listed in the next message. He wants to be asked only for real decisions.
- **Two weeks** (2026-10-03): everything through 2.0 released by 2026-10-17, because another team could ship first.
  Lanes work around the clock, several at once. Speed comes from parallel lanes and trimmed checks, never from
  thinner content: every feature complete, vanilla-quality, finished.
- **Order of the expansions** (2026-10-03): 1.1 villages that build themselves, 1.2 Pokémon and villagers together,
  1.3 Legends, 1.4 edicts and civic items, 1.5 quests become stories, 1.6 threats, 1.7 the realm, 1.8 classes and
  luxuries, 2.0 Wonders.
- **Edicts** (2026-10-03) have real costs, but each has a reform the village earns through quests: once reformed, it
  keeps its boost and loses its cost.
- **Mythic Legends and Wonders** (2026-10-03): several may exist on a server, but each village has a cap, growing with
  its rank (config).
- **Unhappy Legends** (2026-10-03) never move out: they go on strike until their needs are met.
- **The Pokémon tournament** (2026-10-03) must fit the mod's themes (villages, festivals, market days, trainers who
  level up by battling, the chronicle). Still no badges and no gym leaders.
- **Classes** (2026-10-03) switch on for every village on the live server at once.
- **Testing while building** (2026-10-03): builders write their own GameTests as they build; a dedicated QA lane
  tests everything after it lands; slow checks (mutation, repeats, filming) run on GitHub's machines. Releases ship
  verified work only.
- **Release channel** (2026-10-03): 1.0 goes to **CurseForge and GitHub only. Don't publish to Modrinth** (its rules
  bar page images made with AI and may unlist projects made mostly by AI). The pages say the mod was made with AI
  assistance, without saying where. Keep that line general and true: code and textures both had AI help, so never
  "only the code". Store-page work (26.2–26.5) is for CurseForge and GitHub; drop Modrinth parts, including
  mod-publish-plugin's Modrinth target.
- **Villages with no player nearby keep working** (2026-10-03), through chunk tickets; a config option lets a server
  owner pause them instead.

- **Sprint mode** (2026-10-03): the owner asked to go back to how the first chat worked, after four lanes and an
  hourly QA lane built one feature in four days. Two build lanes (odd/even numbers) commit straight to `main` in
  3-hour runs (owner: longer if need be); lane C is off; the QA lane runs overnight only; reviews never block; the evening digest releases daily.

## Milestone 40: The Village Hall, simpler

The owner picked a new layout for the Village Hall screen (2026-10-26, from the design canvas "Village Hall redesign
options", option E and its two "E · Changing a job" and "E · Assigning a bed" boards): a **labeled sidebar** on the
left instead of 18 unlabeled icons, one section at a time on the right, and a **People** table where clicking a
villager opens their details under their row, with buttons to change their job and give them a bed. No expansion
flag: it replaces today's hall screen for everyone the day it lands, so nothing the hall does today may be lost.
Text in American English (36.19). Lane C builds it, in order (each item builds on the one before).
Depends on: nothing open.

## Milestone 41: Waystones

Villages join the Waystones mod's travel network (owner, 2026-10-26): each village raises a waystone by its hall, and
villages that both have one send their caravans and settlers through them. Waystones is in the owner's pack
(`waystones-fabric-1.21.1-21.1.37`, mod id `waystones`); like every mod it is optional: its classes only in
`compat/waystones/`, `modCompileOnly` from the Modrinth maven, listed in `suggests`, never a hard `depends`, and
compat GameTests (`runCompatGameTest`). Without it nothing here appears and nothing breaks. Lane D builds it first.
Depends on: nothing open.

- [x] **41.1** (verified 2026-10-26: 8 new compat tests [WaystoneQaCompatTests]: switch off after the stones stand, one village without a stone, name-tag rename with an odd long name and the cleared name, hall-gone village, travelers' step-in spot, sentences; mutation spot check on VillageWaystones 2/4 killed by existing tests, both survivors now killed; 41.2 waits for B528) (approved 2026-10-26) **A waystone by every Village Hall.** With Waystones installed, a village's builder raises a small
  waystone plaza near the hall (a new blueprint, architect skill and `STYLE.md`, in each village culture's style)
  once the village has a hall, as a normal build the Steward can propose; the stone is the mod's own waystone block,
  named after the village (renamed when the village is), so players who visit can discover it and travel there the
  usual way. A config switch (`villageWaystones`, on) turns it off. Without the mod, the plaza isn't offered. Done
  when: compat GameTests for the plaza built with a working, named waystone, the village renamed, the stone broken
  (the builder repairs it like any build), the switch off, and a GameTest without the mod that nothing is offered;
  blueprint render checked; text in `en_us.json`; wiki page `waystones.md`; scene `village_waystone`.
- [x] **41.2** (verified 2026-10-26: 3 new compat tests [WaystoneMapQaCompatTests]: eight directions and the east/north-east edge, 4 and 5000 blocks, nearest first with the more line, far unloaded village discovered per player, switch off with standing stones; wiki fixed) (approved 2026-11-01) **The hall's Map shows the waystone network.** The hall's Map section (40.1; today's map page until
  40.1 lands) lists the player's villages with a waystone, each with its distance and direction, and marks which
  ones the player has discovered. Done when: compat GameTests for two villages, one undiscovered, one with its stone
  broken; text in `en_us.json`; wiki; scene `hall_waystones`.
- [x] **41.3** (verified 2026-10-26: 8 new compat tests [WaystoneQaCompatTests]: switch off after the stones stand, one village without a stone, name-tag rename with an odd long name and the cleared name, hall-gone village, travelers' step-in spot, sentences; mutation spot check on VillageWaystones 2/4 killed by existing tests, both survivors now killed; 41.2 waits for B528) (approved 2026-10-27) **Caravans and settlers travel by waystone.** Between two villages that both have a waystone, trade
  caravans and settlers walk to their stone and step out at the other village's (with the mod's own sound and
  particles) instead of walking the whole way; if either stone is missing or broken, they walk as today. Done when:
  compat GameTests for a caravan and a settler going through, a stone broken mid-trip (they walk), save and reload
  mid-trip; text; wiki; scene `waystone_caravan`.

- 2026-10-27 (lane-c-1027-2153, B641, root cause and decisions): **Cause**: the owner's Terrace was planned from the modded library (37.12; herringbone floor in the shot) before B281, when the spots file had six spots (west table and chair, four beds): B281 inserted the east kitchen's table and chair (indices 2, 3) before the beds, so the saved choice (37.3, keyed by spot index) had no piece for that kitchen (spruce stand-ins kept) and `FurnitureChoice.apply` dropped all four beds' pieces as mismatched (index and place no longer agreed); a build's choice is never re-chosen, so B281's fix never reached it, and the modded library has no shipped history, so it showed no Refresh either. The "crockery on a wall shelf" is the library's `handcrafted:wood_crockery_combo`, which `modded_library.py` puts in the cell over a table spot's top cell: over a fence table that is a block above the pressure plate (the plate is 1/16 thick), and once the table is swapped for a one-block Handcrafted table the plate's cell is air, so it hung a block up in both kitchens (`Resting.reseat` only set vanilla pots and candles down). The half is not placed mirrored and the floating check skips no half: both halves are drawn and furnished alike today (new tests, turned and mirrored). **Fix**: `apply` finds a saved piece's spot by place and kind when its index moved; `FurnitureChoice.staleFor` tells a choice made against an older spots file, and `Refreshes` then offers "Refresh to the latest look" from today's drawing itself (key `latest`, the vanilla or modded copy as built), which furnishes the missing spots as a new build (B642's `refreshedFor`) and swaps the stand-ins; the library's pieces over a swapped table are set down on it (`Resting.libraryPiece`), and over a table left vanilla left out (`Resting.offThinTops`). No saved field added, nothing renamed. `FurnishingTableGameTests.aPieceWhoseSpotIsGoneBuildsVanilla`'s past-the-end piece now stands where no spot is (a stale index with a spot's place and kind is that spot by design), and the test also checks such a piece lands on its spot. **Decisions**: (1) standing builds are fixed only through the Repairs page's Refresh, as 36.21 does (37.3: a standing build never changes by itself); (2) a choice whose spots file only gained spots at the end (no index moved) can't be told from one left vanilla on purpose, so it isn't offered; (3) the old crockery hanging over a vanilla table comes away in that refresh (the build as built is matched with the old placement, `applyAsBuilt` without the set-down). (needs owner check: on the live server open the Village Hall's Repairs page, press Refresh on that Terrace, and look at both kitchens: a Handcrafted table and chair in each, crockery on the tables.)
- 2026-10-27 (lane-b subagent, B642, root cause and decisions): **Cause**: a furnished build's saved furniture (37.3) is keyed by spot index and place in the spots file of the day it was built, and B260 redrew the Stone House's spots (clock, table and chairs moved, spots added), so the refresh applied the saved pieces against TODAY's file: they matched nothing, the older drawing came out unfurnished, the pieces standing (table, chairs, Cozy Home clock) read as the player's and stayed, and today's new spots got vanilla pieces on top (the second table). A vanilla build refreshed correctly (shown by the new tests on the old code: only the furnished case failed). **Fix**: the older drawing is furnished with the saved pieces where they were put (`FurnitureChoice.applyAsBuilt`), and the current one with the choice brought to today's spots (`refreshedFor`: a piece kept where one of the same kind already stands, other spots furnished as a new build); the finished refresh saves that choice. No new saved field: works on the live saves as they are. (1) The 37.12 modded-library copies have no shipped history (`history.py` skips `modded/`), so a build from the modded library shows no Refresh rather than being diffed against today's copy (before, the old drawing was silently replaced by today's copy); ship `blueprint_history/modded/...` when the modded library opens. (2) Lucky's Cozy Home can't load in the dev compat run, so the compat test uses Handcrafted; the clock's case is covered by the test-pieces table in `RefreshMatchesFreshBuildGameTests`. (3) Scene `refresh_old_house` now starts from the drawing before B260 (the owner's), vanilla furniture (the screenshot client has no furniture mods without -Pfurniture).
- 2026-10-27 (lane-b subagent, 36.22, decisions): (1) **Depth steps**: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 for every miner (Novice and Apprentice stop at 64); 96 for Journeyman and up; 128 for Expert and up; "down to just above bedrock" (the world's floor + 5, Y=-59 in the Overworld, the floor every quarry already kept to) for Master only. The marker cycles 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 96, 128, bedrock, then the strip mines; the bedrock choice is saved as `depth: -1`. (2) A marker deeper than the miner's level is **taken, not refused**: the pit is cut off at their depth (counted from the marked top), the player is told which level the full depth needs, and nothing below is dug. The level asked is the real pit's (a 128 marker cut off by the world's floor at 90 deep needs only a Journeyman). (3) Leveling up mid-quarry: every work tick `Miners.deepen` takes the floor down to the new level's reach (the pit is dug top-down, so the digging order and the stair just carry on), and the owner hears it; a quarry finished short says so, and the marker comes back with its depth to hand over again. Strip mines are unaffected. (4) Saves: a cut-off quarry saves `wanted_bottom`; absent (every older save) it is the box's own floor, so saved quarries keep their depth. (5) A pit more than 64 deep measures its reach from the middle of its top, not the 3D center (a bedrock pit under a hill would otherwise read too far: see the 36.20 QA note below; pits up to 64 are measured as before). (6) Two tests asserted the old five depths (`MinerGameTests.quarryMarkerOffersStripMinesDownAShaft`, `QaStageFourGameTests.quarryDepthChosenBySneakClicksOnTheAir`): updated to the new cycle in full, not loosened. (7) The test world's tests stand on the superflat floor, so the deep tests build the pit as a column above the area: the upper layers already dug with their steps standing, the bottom layers real rock the miner digs (`DeepQuarryGameTests`).
- 2026-10-26 (qa-lane-b-1026-2138, 36.20, QA): a quarry's reach is measured from the 3D center of the dug box, depth included (strip-mine shafts aside), so a 64-deep quarry marked 125 blocks out reads about 129 and is refused while the player sees 125 on the ground. Same as the old 64-block limit, so not filed as a bug; left as is unless the owner wants only the distance across to count. Not tested: a far site in unloaded chunks (the test player keeps chunks loaded).
- 2026-10-26 (lane-b-1026-1838, 36.21, decisions): (1) No build recorded which drawing it was built from or what the Builder placed, so "the build's own record" is the older drawing itself: the mod now ships every earlier version of each blueprint changed since 1.0 (2026-10-17) and every version of the Stone House line (`data/aliveworkplace/blueprint_history/<blueprint>/<commit>.nbt`, 165 files, from `tools/blueprints/history.py`; rerun it after a redraw), and a finished build is matched to the one it still stands closest to (spots where the drawings differ, as drawn by the old minus as drawn by the new). A block standing as that drawing drew it is the Builder's; anything else is a player's and stays. (2) The button lives on the Repairs page, which is the Buildings section's (40.1), listed after the repairs; the list click shows what changes (New / Taken away, by decorations, furniture pieces and blocks), the Brush button hands it over. (3) A refresh is a repair site with `refresh_from` set, starting in CLEAR (the Builder's usual clearing keeps containers and claimed beds); job blocks are left out of its list too. Its lists are worked out again from the world on load. (4) "Nearest free Builder" means one who looks after the build (hired by its owner or a friend), as for repairs; with none, `refresh_asked` is saved and the first such Builder free takes it up on their next round, whatever builderRepairs says. (5) Modded-furniture variants (`structure/modded/`) and imported builds have no shipped history: no button.
- 2026-10-26 (lane-b-1026-1838, 36.20, decisions): (1) "The village's claimed area" is the hall's radius (`VillageHalls.RADIUS`, a circle across, any height, so a quarry's pit below counts) plus every cell painted into one of its City Plan zones; the worker's block must stand in it (the nearest hall within its radius), and a spot in it is in reach whatever the distance (`work/Reach`). A worker in no village has only the long reach. (2) One key per area job: `quarryReach`, `fieldReach`, `treeFarmReach`, `orchardAreaReach` (not `orchardReach`, beside the older `orchardRadius`), `berryPlotReach`, 16 to 256, default 128; `maxSiteDistance` keeps its key, default 48 to 128. (3) Config format 5: a file of before holding exactly the old default 48 moves to 128 (as format 4 did for `villagerElderDays`); any other number stays. (4) The rule also covers who the Steward's desk, the City Plan's pieces and upgrades, the Founder and the Grand Rebuild pick as builder, RepairAsks and Roads, and the Steward's plot search (a table in the hall's village reaches every zone). The builder's helper recruiting (`Builders.recruit`, bench to bench) keeps the plain distance, now 128. (5) Existing tests whose numbers the spec changes were updated: 48/64 reaches to 128, and the sentence matchers accept "outside <village> and" (a hall an earlier batch left can put a test's table in a village); PlotGameTests' "22 blocks off" now fits (the table is in the village) and QaStewardPlots' inclusive-reach test uses a hall radius of 20 to leave its tables outside the village. (6) Left as it was: the placed Blueprint's supply report and tooltip look for the nearest table within `maxSiteDistance` (128), so in a village wider than that a table farther off isn't named there (the build is still taken when handed over).

- 2026-10-11 (35.5, lane-c-1011-2132): **Crews** decisions: (1) "8 × 8 columns" is read as the part split at least 8 by 8
  (a column is the part's width over 8, rounded down, at least one block): a 64-wide part gets the 8-block columns the
  spec names, and the 9-wide test folly 1-block columns, so eight builders have room (8-block columns would give the
  folly four columns and four idle builders; 2-block ones left the eight at a third of one builder's time, not a
  quarter). The layer rule doesn't apply to levelling the ground (its list isn't in layers), and a block the lead gave
  up on (out of reach) doesn't hold the layers back, else a crew could wait on it for ever. (2) The lead of stage I is the Master Architect when he is one of the village's
  builders, else the builder handed the plan; each next stage goes to the Master Architect or the highest-level of
  the lead and the village's free builders. (3) "Call every builder" is a clickable line under the stone's status
  (`/workplace wonders call`, owner or operator within 8 blocks); a called builder joins between builds, ahead of its
  own queue, until the Wonder is done. (4) The test folly's file now allows a crew of 12 (was 4) so eight and ten
  builders fit. (5) A crew forms only on a Wonder's parts; the old 64-step helper window is unchanged for other builds,
  and `workplaceBuildersHelp` helpers no longer join a Wonder's parts (the crew does). **Not tested: the PERF
  benchmark with a 12-builder crew** (Done when's third line): `/workplace benchmark` and `tools/packtest` set up plots
  of ordinary workers and have no way to start a Wonder, and the pack's jar has Wonders behind the closed 2.0 gate, so
  a crew can't be put on the pack server without new harness code (a `benchmark` option that opens the gate and begins
  the folly with 12 builders). Left for the QA lane; the GameTests measure the crew's speed, not its tick cost.
  **The quarter, met (lane-c-1012-0333):** see the end of this note. Before that: `WonderCrewGameTests.eightBuildersRaiseTheFolly` times one builder alone on
  the folly (12,372 to 12,416 ticks at `workplaceBuildDelay` 20, against 11,940 for its 597 blocks) and then eight on
  the same ground: 3,440 to 3,600 ticks over four runs, a third of the lone time or less but not the quarter (3,100)
  the Done when asks. Members are busy 73 to 85% of their ticks, yet take about 34 ticks a block against the lone
  builder's 21: the time goes on walking between columns and to the chests and dodging each other, not on waiting
  for layers (tried here without effect: 1-block or 2-block columns, taking for a whole column per trip, a crew member
  keeping its bag while it waits, its pause running on while it walks). Stage I's walls take 1,500 to 1,650 ticks,
  levelling the ground round stage III about 360. The test holds the crew to a third until this is solved; make it
  a quarter then. Fixed after the first full build (15 dome blocks missing): the lead of a crew reached its retries
  while the crew was still building below and gave up for good on blocks with nothing to hang on yet; now, while the
  crew has work, the lead puts those to the back of its retries instead. That wasn't the cause (lane-c-1012-0033,
  2 to 3 failures in 8 runs of the test alone, with logging): the lead fell off the dome ("hit the ground too hard")
  during stage III, `Builders.onBuilderDeath` removed its part's site, and a Wonder counts a part whose site is gone
  as built, so the Wonder finished with the dome's top never put up. Now a Wonder part outlives its lead
  (`WonderCrews.handOn`): it goes to the highest-level member of its crew, else the lead a next stage would get (in
  their queue), else the first builder to join; a member's death just leaves its column. Decision (lane-c-1012-0033):
  **a builder on its job takes no fall damage** (`BuilderEvents`, any build, not only Wonders): builders work on walls,
  roofs and domes like professionals on scaffolds, and a crew jostling at the dome's edge lost 1 to 2 of 8 builders a
  run to falls. Why they go over the edge (crewmates bumping, `hop`) isn't fixed; with the rule it costs a little
  time, not a builder. `handOn` itself is now a safety net for other deaths (mobs, lava) and is not tested by a
  GameTest of its own: with handOn but still with fall deaths, 2 of 10 runs stuck at stage 3, 0%, cause not found. Everything else of the Done when is met and tested (columns, layers, nothing hung in the air, the
  reload, scene `wonder_crew`).
  **Finished (lane-c-1012-0333):** after the merge the crew took 3,920 to 4,220 ticks (4 runs; the full build's 4,140
  failed even the third). Measured where the members' ticks went: (1) each took for the rest of its own 1-block column
  only, a block or two, so it walked to the chests for nearly every block (stage III: down from the dome and back up,
  about 600 of its 750 ticks), and the lead, taking for the 192 steps a lone builder takes for, emptied the chests for
  the rest; (2) levelling the ground round stage III with no dirt in the chests deferred one hole a tick, 360 ticks of a
  whole crew standing about (a lone builder too). Fixes in `BuilderWork`: a crew member (the lead too) takes in one trip
  for its column and a share of the stage dealt round the crew like cards, each step to half the crew, plus a little of
  the later stages (`crewShare`); a builder out of a material while levelling skips every hole wanting it at once
  (`outForLandscape`, for any build). Tried and dropped (worse in 6-run A/B tests): picking columns it has the
  materials for (3,449 mean against 3,220), taking from a near crewmate before the chests (3,764 to 4,091), an exact
  n-th share (3,245) against half (2,772) or all (2,944). Now: crew alone 2,539 to 2,878 ticks over 10 runs (mean
  2,665), lone builder about 12,150, so the quarter (3,037) holds with 5 to 16% to spare; the test asks a quarter and
  passed 14 of 14 full runs. `handOn` now has its GameTest (`aLeadKilledMidPartHandsItOn`, 8 of 8): the lead killed
  mid-part, the part goes to a living member as its lead and the folly is finished; the dead lead's bag drops where it
  fell, so the test has the owner put it back in a chest by the stone (without that the crew waits, rightly, for the
  materials it carried). **Still not run: the PERF benchmark with a 12-builder crew** (above): left for the QA lane.
  Seen while testing, not this item's: `WonderDataGameTests.theCapsHold` fails ("a limit of 2 refused the second
  village") when only the six Wonder test classes run, also without these changes (the other classes' follies count
  against its server limit); it passes in the full suite.

  (0.78 / 4.62 / 9.10 emeralds a day), 37 containers and 2,037 items equal on loading, daycare boarders, the fossil
  revival, the parcel in transit and the build in STRUCTURE all kept; log audit exit 0 (pack registry errors only).
  **Found and fixed:** a config file written while a gate was closed holds `false` for its switches, so the first
  rehearsal opened with classes off (as the owner's server would have): `WorkplaceConfig.parse` now gives such switches
  their new default (the file records `expansionsOpen`; a format-2 file, 0.139.0 to 0.142.0, counts as all closed; config
  format 3), `ExpansionGateGameTests.aFileFromBeforeTheReleaseTakesTheNewDefaults`.
  Decisions: (1) the old jar is the v0.142.0 tag built with `command/Rehearsal.java` copied in (the published jar
  can't seed); (2) "1.8" is run as main with `-Daliveworkplace.shots=true` (every gate open; M34 is still false);
  (3) takings are compared with a control (the saved world on the old jar for the same 2 days), since they drift by

  beds in the open, so everyone seeds as a Peasant. Open: the 1 s worst tick in the seeding window needs a JFR profile

- **Fire and the Firewarden (32.16, lane-b-1011-1233, 2026-10-11): decisions.** `village_fire.json` is a disaster
  file (so `disasters` switches it) whose daily roll never starts it (`chance` 0, no `fires_a_day`): its fires are
  short events kept per village in memory, set off by its `ignition` block (lightning 0.334, chimney 0.02 while
  `dry_days` 5 or a drought is under way, burning arrows 0.25 from raider-tagged shooters). "Likelier the more wood":
  the `when` gate (wood share 0.3) and two `factors` of 1.25 (at 0.5 and 0.7). In a village a fire with no builders'
  block left beside it goes out at age 15 (else it smoulders on a player's roof forever); the brigade's bell swings
  and rings without vanilla's ring (which sends villagers to hide); a new Firewarden has both buckets full; builders
  skip a build with fire within 16 blocks. The guide page `docs/guide/fire.md` went in now, as 32.14's lines did,
  though M32 is still closed: the release that opens M32 should check it.

- **A day's warning (32.14, lane-b-1011-0933, 2026-10-11): the Seer is not a source yet.** The spec skips the Seer
  until M29's Seer item lands; besides, with a Seer in the village the night is foretold at dawn by the Seer's own
  round (29.16), which bypasses the threat clock, and the clock rolls only one day ahead, so two days' warning needs
  the clock to roll two nights. Decided: `guard/Warnings.SOURCES` is the list other systems add to; the Seer joins
  when its item lands, with the clock rolling a night further for it.

- 2026-10-05 (27.15, decisions; lane c): roads are built only with a Steward appointed at the hall (and `steward` on),
  and not while the plan is set to Rest; with `stewardRoads` off (and in GameTests, which the road tests turn on) the
  plan's roads are drawn but never routed or built. A road's way (`CityPlan.Road.route`, offsets from the hall with y,
  saved with `routed` and the `built` segment numbers; older saves load unrouted) is found once per road and kept, so
  a reload doesn't route again; a road changed on the plan is a new road. A stretch that finds no way (or takes over
  30,000 nodes) ends the road there. "Kept clear" is the road's whole width at each node: natural ground or paving
  underneath (or a one-block dip onto it), only air, plants, leaves or natural ground (dug away) for 3 blocks over,
  no water; buildings (finished, or sites) are kept off a block wider. The segment id is
  `roads/<hall x_y_z>/<road key>_<n>` (the key a hash of the road and its route), not a running number, so it needs
  no new saved counter. A segment's columns go to the nearest node (straight across first), its surface at that node's
  ground height: the middle mix, the edge mix on the outermost column (a lane is all middle), stairs where the next or
  last node is a block lower, facing the climb. Road styles map from building styles by `blueprint_styles` in each file
  (Stonework also paves Grand; any other style is As drawn); 27.4's style names are kept. "No building of the village
  waits" is read as: no Steward's build queued or without a builder; a segment goes to the nearest idle builder
  (nothing building, nothing queued) whose bench is within `Builders.MAX_SITE_DISTANCE`. Segments are sites owned by
  the hall's owner but not the Steward's open builds (no `stewardHall`), so they don't take his build slots; they
  don't level the ground round them. A finished segment gives the builder 2 XP (like a repair), no blueprint back and
  no chronicle line; the whole road finished gets one ("Bram finished a Stonework road, 40 blocks long"). A door's lane
  is a road on the plan with `lane` (approved, 1 wide, the joined road's style), built like the others; lanes don't
  count towards the 24 roads (at most 64 lanes). Lamps, bridges and the slab use of steps wait for 27.16 (the style
  files already name their blocks).
- 2026-10-05 (27.16, decisions; lane c): lamps and bridges are part of a road's segment blueprints, so a builder lays
  them with the road and nothing new is saved per lamp. A street or avenue's lamp is the `street_lamp` blueprint styled
  like the road (`BlueprintStyles.styled`, the road style's `lamp` swapped in for its lanterns), its foot a block beside
  the road's edge, at nodes 16, 32, 48... alternating left and right of the way the road runs, plus one 3 nodes before
  each place it enters another road ("at every crossing"). A lamp needs clear natural ground for its 3x3 foot off every
  road and no door within 2 blocks of it; else it moves up to 3 nodes on, or is left out (so corners and bridges get
  none). Lanes get the style's `lantern_post` two high with the lamp on top every 12 nodes. Beauty counts the lamps on
  finished segments (`Road.lamps`, saved, default 0) at a Street Lamp's 1 point each, inside the same 10% cap; the light
  is real block light, so the "dark" tip sees it with no change. Gaps: each stretch's straight line is looked along
  before routing; a column with water on top, or no ground within 2 blocks under the surface, starts a gap, which runs
  straight on along the line's main axis to the first column with ground (40 at most). Up to 16 wide it is bridged:
  the deck is one block over the higher bank (the spec's "at the banks' height" read as on top of them, so the deck
  clears the water and the first and last deck blocks are the stairs up, the "ramp"), rails (the style's wall/fence) on
  both sides, a pillar under the middle of every 4th deck block down to the bed, 12 deep at most. Wider, the road ends
  at the near bank, the width is saved on the road (`Road.gap`, default 0) and the Steward's card on the desk says "A
  road stops at a gap 20 blocks wide: a bridge spans 16 at most". Banks of different heights are not evened out (a
  drop of 2 off the deck's low end is possible). Steps: 27.15's stairs already run across the road's whole width; the
  style's slab is still unused. Crossings: columns another routed road also covers are paved with the middle mix (no
  edge stripe through the crossing).

  from 16 words (Ember, Gilded, Starlit…), picked from the maker and the day so it never changes. If the Legend's slot
  was taken during the mood, the Masterwork is still made but nobody becomes the Legend. Switching `strangeMoods` off
  calls a mood already on off quietly at its next check (no sulk). A broken workstation doesn't end the mood: the
  chest by its spot still counts. The Founder's way (`"founder": true`) is skipped by the daily roll: 29.23 starts it
