- **27.5 decisions** (lane-c-1004-1832, 2026-10-04): the City Plan appoints through its own handler (`city/Stewards.appoint`, called from BuilderEvents before the Stations items) rather than a `work/Stations.ALL` entry: a Stations entry would let `Stations.choose` give the nearest free hall whichever hall the plan is bound to, and every list built from `ALL` (guide pages, job-item texts, the workstation break counter) would change with it; the appointment still uses `Stations.assign`. "Standing by the hall" is within `Stations.REACH` + 1 blocks. His rounds visit one spot per zone of the plan (the zone's cell nearest the hall), the storehouse and his open sites (`StewardWork.OPEN_SITES`, empty until 27.6); which zones count as "empty" is left to 27.6's planner. `StewardWork.PLANNER` is the hook 27.6–27.9 replace (it returns the status line, "Looking over the City Plan" until then); `Stewards.credit` gives XP for builds/jobs (`XP_BUILD` 10, `XP_JOB` 3). Old halls: a saved `stewardPlaceChecked` flag on the hall's block entity makes the first tick after loading re-register a record with 0 free places once.
- **27.6 decisions** (lane-c-1004-2132, 2026-10-04): rule files follow docs/design/M27.md's shape (`{"beds_short": {"at_least": 1}}`, `"do": {"build": {...}}`); `{"not": {...}}` turns any condition round (the starter Hearth rule uses it). Every field is checked and an unknown one refuses the file (`field 'when[0].beds_short.at_least'` in the warning), so a typo can't silently do nothing. Each condition gives one number, and `why` is filled with those in the rule's order (`%2$s` for the second). `cooldown_days` and `max` count from when a wish is *carried out*: 27.7–27.9 call `StewardWishes.carriedOut(level, hall, rule)`, which counts it, starts the cooldown and drops the wish; until then a rule that holds is wished for every morning. The day's wishes (at most 8, highest priority first) are ranked by `StewardWork.PLANNER` the first time he is at the hall each day (his day is `dayTime / 24000`, as his rounds) and saved on the hall as `steward` (absent in older halls: none). `store_full` reads the Storehouses' chests only (slots taken / all slots, via the new `ItemStores.slots`). `upgrade_available`'s `blueprint` is optional (any building). `VillageAdvice` now exposes the numbers its tips use (`bedsShort`, `foodWanted`, `jobless`, `poiCount`, `upgradable`, `homes`) and both read them.
- **27.7 decisions** (lane-c-1004-2132, 2026-10-04): "ground within 4 blocks of level" is read as the ground under the footprint rising at most 4 from its lowest to its highest column (so a slope of 6 is refused whatever its shape), and the plot's floor is the median ground height; columns above it must be natural ground down to it. "A builder's Blueprint Table" counts both builder job sites (Blueprint Table and Builder's Bench). The footprint plus 2 also stays off the plan's roads (as wide as drawn), so a house never stands on a street before 27.15 builds it. A column is read from its top down; a player's block above the ground (a roof, a wall, a chest) refuses the plot only if it's inside the box, so an overhang or a ceiling far above doesn't. "The rule's next blueprint" is `Plots.Request.blueprints` (a list, tried in order at each spot); 27.6's rules hold one, so it's a list of one until a rule format lists more. Spots are tried a few per cell (every `cellSize/2` blocks), nearest the hall first, each with its four turns, as drawn then mirrored. Results live in memory (`Plots.request`/`Plots.result`, not saved): the planner asks each morning for every build wish, and a search starts again only when the plan's zones or roads, the tables in reach or the builds in the plan's area change. 27.8 reads `Plots.result` for its proposal and calls `StewardWishes.carriedOut`.

  no worn tools** (33.3's Remedies note; `Board.counts`), and the Remedies icon is a healing potion. (7) **The

- **39.7a design** (lane-e-1018-1612, 2026-10-18): real Create trains. The village whose hall key sorts first puts its own Create train together at its station once Create's railway knows both stations on one network: a small bogey on the track past the station, train casing and the caravan's chest at bogey height, a seat between two train controls (one each way) above, glued with super glue, a jobless villager seated as conductor, assembled by the station (`StationBlockEntity.assemble`) and given a cyclic Create schedule (destination, 10 s wait, back). Decision on the goods (changed by 39.7b, lane-e-1018-1912): the caravan waits at the station (`BOARDING`); when the train stands there its goods go into the carriage's chest, Create's mounted storage, all or nothing (`IN_CHEST`; no room: as the caravan's record, `ABOARD`), and at the other station what is still in the chest of them comes out and is what's delivered (never the record, so goods a player took from the chest at a station aren't paid twice). Train gone or the far station gone while they're in the chest: what a derailed train still holds comes back out for the timed trip; a train broken up keeps them in its chest (a player breaking it up at a station gets the chest back with them) and the caravan is taken off the road with a chronicle line, so they're neither lost nor doubled. Without a free villager, before assembly or after a player breaks the train up, caravans take 39.7's timed trip. Village trains are found by their owner, `CaravanTrains.railwayId`, so players' trains are never touched. Stations the village aims face the other village (Create stops trains at a station from one side; facing away, no path is found). Create classes only in `compat/create/` (`CreateTrains`, behind `CaravanTrains.RAILWAY`); the mod compiles against libs/ with `modCompileOnly` (`tests.compat_compile_files`). 39.7b: the track along a road is one line trains can run (`CaravanTrains.plan`: Create's trains only pass between pieces that meet nearly straight, `TrackEdge.canTravelTo` wants a dot of 0.875, so Create's ascending piece next to a level one never carries a train; each run of steps is one sloped Create curve between level landings, at least two blocks along per block up, and each turn a curve between straight pieces 2-3 nodes off it); the train's blocks are a generated blueprint a builder builds (bogey placed with railway casing), then glued and assembled. Still not done: joining a Train Station build that stands off the road to the road's track (the stations must stand beside the road's track today); a one-block dip, a step on a turn or a zig-zag (the road's A* routes in steps of one block, so a diagonal road zig-zags) stay gaps, and the railway then never joins.
- **39.7d design (lane-e-1019-0113)** (2026-10-19): the Conductor. A villager job, `aliveworkplace:conductor`, registered only with Create (like the Mechanic, `ModVillagers.CONDUCTOR`, null without it; a saved Conductor in a world without Create loads jobless). Workstation: Create's own Train Station (`create:track_station`, POI `aliveworkplace:track_station`, optional entry of `acquirable_job_site`), as Create's Toolbox is the Mechanic's: no new block (the owner's "fewer job blocks", 21.1a), the village already has the station, and a jobless villager by it takes it by themselves; so the Train Station blueprint needs no workstation spot. Behind `villageTrains` (M39's gate), no switch of its own: off, `WorkerLimits.hideFull` hides stations from the jobless (Conductors already hired keep the job). The seat: `CaravanTrains.conductorFor`, the nearest grown-up Conductor within 24 blocks of the station not already riding, else the nearest jobless villager as before (existing trains and saves untouched). Off the train he works his station the vanilla way (no work package). Calling the stop: `CaravanTrains.calls` from `serve`, when a train seen away from a station stands there, the Conductor riding it says "Now arriving at <village>! All change, mind the gap." over his head (WorkerStatus) and in the chat of players within 24 blocks; in memory only (a train first seen standing, as after a restart, isn't called), no chronicle line (a train going back and forth would flood it); a jobless driver says nothing. Riders are found by id: Create may save a carriage's riders and put them back as new entities on the way. Trades (`ModTrades.conductorTrades`): coal for emeralds, rails, Create track, powered rails, train schedule, track signals, railway casing, train controls (Create's by id). Outfit: maroon peaked cap with gold band and badge, maroon tunic with brass buttons, watch chain, ticket punch, black gloves (`tools/textures/art/villagers_2.py` `conductor`). Showcase: the `village_train` scene now has a Conductor at Thornholm's station who rides the train and calls the stop at Ashford.
